summary: Every claim written as `mission-run/RUN` is decided against the run's declared `authority` intersected with its starter's; the new daemon setting `[programs] authority` (default `audit`) records a write outside it as `rule.audited` on `rule/run-authority`, or refuses it with `run-authority-denied` when set to `enforce`

replay.detail: No claim kind or projection change. Audit records reuse `rule.audited` with `rule` set to `run-authority`. A child run a program starts writes its `mission-run.created` and initial `run-generation.created` with actor `mission-run/PARENT`; its `requester` stays the parent's.

schema.detail: No table, index or migration change.

rules.detail: First enforced declared authority. Writes by `mission-run/*` actors are checked at write admission: `mission.published` needs `publish`, a run's creation and initial generation need `start`, a later generation needs `revise`, any other claim needs `write` on its subject; a run always journals `program.step` on its own step runs. The effective authority is the current revision's block intersected with the starter's (recursively through program-started parents); a person, agent or daemon starter's enforce-mode rules also decide each write. Writers that are not runs are untouched. Audit is the default.

compatibility.detail: New optional config table `[programs]` with `authority = "audit" | "enforce"`; an older build refuses a config that sets it (unknown field), so set it only on builds that read it. Nothing writes as a run until the program engine dispatches with run credentials.

downtime.detail: The mode is read when the daemon starts; changing it needs a restart.

manual.detail: No operator action is required. Read `fractal rules audit run-authority` before setting `enforce`.

recovery.detail: Set `[programs] authority = "audit"` (or remove the table) and restart to let refused writes proceed again.
